# Reference data

The primary source is NOAA/NASA/USAF, [U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976, NASA-TM-X-74335 / NOAA-S/T-76-1562](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19770009539). The fixtures were read from page images of [NOAA's copy, including the appended errata correspondence](https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/stp/space-weather/online-publications/miscellaneous/us-standard-atmosphere-1976/us-standard-atmosphere_st76-1562_noaa.pdf), downloaded on 2026-11-04. The SHA-256 of that 18,267,064-byte PDF is `820a1d7c6bd533e3a845696601cc74013d7d851babac4dab35bee3b1feae35cf`. The source is a U.S. government work; NTRS permits public use.

`source_page` means the printed page number, not the PDF viewer's page index. Numerical reference values come from the report or the separately identified equation calculation below, never from this Go implementation. The scan's embedded text is unsuitable for extracting the tables. OCR was used to locate rows; values were read visually, and discrepancies were reread from enlarged row images before accepting or correcting a transcription. The checked-in fixtures make tests independent of network access and OCR software.

| File | Source | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `geometric.csv` | Part 4, Table I, printed pp. 51–73 | 157 geometric heights, −5 to 1,000 km; temperature, pressure, density |
| `secondary.csv` | Part 4, Table II, pp. 77–97 | 9 heights, 0 to 1,000 km; geopotential height, gravity, total number density, molar mass |
| `species.csv` | Part 4, Table VIII, pp. 210–215 | 38 heights, 86 to 1,000 km; N₂, O, O₂, Ar, He, H |
| `transport.csv` | Part 4, Table III, pp. 99–115 | 18 heights, −5 to 80 km; sound speed, dynamic viscosity, kinematic viscosity |
| `molar_mass_ratios.csv` | Part 1, Table 8, p. 9; precise 86 km ratio in §1.2.6, p. 10 | All 13 geometric-height ratios at 500 m spacing |
| `thermal_conductivity.csv` | Part 1, Eq. (53), p. 19 | 10 temperatures, 186.8673–320.676 K; an independent 60-digit decimal calculation |

Table I pressure is converted from millibars to pascals and Table II molar mass from kg/kmol to kg/mol. All other transcribed table fields preserve their printed values and precision. Some Table II pages label the first altitude column `H` despite the geometric-altitude caption; the numerical pairs consistently put geometric altitude first and the smaller positive geopotential height second, matching Table I and the defining conversion. The fixtures follow those numerical pairs. A hydrogen entry of zero below 150 km denotes the model's omitted hydrogen component, shown as `1−∞` in Table VIII. It does not mean real atmospheric hydrogen is absent.

Part 1, §1.2.4, p. 9 explicitly states that the main tables below 86 km omitted the molecular-weight adjustment. It instructs readers to multiply tabulated temperature and molar mass by Table 8's `M/M₀`, and to divide number density by that ratio between 80 and 86 km. The temperature comparisons apply this independent tabulated correction at the affected heights. At 86 km, Table I already uses the upper-atmosphere kinetic temperature. The ratio at 86 km uses the more precise `0.9995788` from §1.2.6, rather than Table 8's rounded `0.999579`. Separate tests retain the more precise species boundary values from Part 1, Table 9, the geopotential layer boundaries, and the sea-level values from Table 10.

The main tables' thermal-conductivity column has a factor-of-1,000 error discussed in the appended correspondence. Scaling it alone does not make it an accurate Eq. (53) reference: the sea-level entry is `2.5362e-5`, while Eq. (53) gives approximately `2.5325884e-2` W/(m K). The conductivity fixture therefore uses the defining equation with Python's standard-library `decimal` arithmetic at 60-digit precision, independently of Go's binary floating-point operations. Regenerate it with `python3 scripts/generate_thermal_reference.py` from the repository root. Python is unnecessary for running the Go tests.

The tests check fixture schemas, row counts, finite values, and strictly increasing coordinates. Temperature tolerances are 0.0006 K below 86 km and 0.006 K above it, reflecting three- versus two-decimal tabulation. Relative comparison budgets are 0.01% for pressure and viscosity, and 0.05% for density, species, and total number density. The wider pressure budget accommodates the original table's rounding/truncation, including the 16 km entry; it is not a numerical integration error estimate. Gravity permits 0.001% relative error, geopotential height 0.51 m absolute, and molar mass 0.2% relative to account for the coarsest three-digit Table II entries. Sound speed permits 0.006 m/s. The Eq. (53) comparisons use a `1e-14` relative tolerance. [Measured deviations and interpretation](../docs/validation.md) distinguish these test budgets from observed error and atmospheric variability.
